transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Well… they brought me in, mostly. It was at the fair, you know, the one with the tractors all lined up by the feed tent—my nephew used to show calves there, good calves too—and I was giving this little talk, or supposed to be.

I got up on the tractor and started moving the controls, jerking them around to show everybody the new pattern. I kept saying they needed to see it right, that the rows line up different if you understand the motion. People were yelling at me to stop, but I just… I couldn’t make myself stop. My hands kept doing it. So now I’m here.
Did you hear or see anything unusual while you were on the tractor that others might not have heard or seen?

Yeah… not so much on the tractor right then, or—well, maybe it all runs together. But out by the north pasture, especially when it’s getting toward dusk and the light goes flat, I hear voices real clear coming up from the irrigation lines.

They’ll say which rows are poisoned and which ones are blessed. It sounds like it’s right in the pipes, like water talking through metal. And that’s not just when I’m all wound up either… it happens other weeks too. The north pasture’s always had strange drainage, my dad used to complain about it, but this is different.
Did you feel like your thoughts were connected and made sense to you when you were giving the talk on the tractor?

At the time it felt connected to me, like I was laying it out plain. But when I try to explain the plan, it gets… tangled up. I start with the soil carbon, then the bank men, then the satellites watching the fields, then seed genetics and county politics, and somehow I don’t get back to what folks actually asked me.

People say, “That’s not what we asked,” or they look at each other like I’ve wandered off. But to me it feels like it all belongs together.
Have you been using any alcohol or drugs around the time of the incident at the fair?

I don’t know… I mean, I wasn’t thinking about that. They sell beer over by the grandstand sometimes, and my cousin used to say you can tell a county fair by the smell of diesel and fried dough, but around the tractor—no, I’m not sure what all you’re asking.

I didn’t keep track of anything like that. It wasn’t like I had a list in my head of what I’d had or hadn’t had. The day just kind of went sideways.
Did you drink any alcohol on the day of the incident at the fair?

I’m not real sure. I mean, I don’t remember sitting there thinking, “I had a beer” or “I didn’t.” At the fair there’s always folks walking around with cups, and the beer tent’s not far from the tractor pulls some years, but that day… it all got mixed up in my head.

I can’t give you a clean yes or no on it.
Do you often find it difficult to stay on topic when talking to others?

Yeah… I guess I do. I don’t mean to. I’ll start answering what somebody asked, but then the pieces all start connecting in my head.

Like with the plan, I try to explain it and it comes out all tangled—soil carbon, the bank men, satellites over the fields, seed genetics, county politics—and then folks say, “That’s not what I asked,” because I never make it back around to the question. In my mind it’s all part of the same thing, but I can see people getting lost.
Do you often find yourself jumping from one idea to another when talking, without finishing your initial thought?

Yeah… that happens. I’ll start with one thing and then another piece grabs onto it, like I’m trying to explain the plan and suddenly I’m talking about soil carbon, then the bank men, then satellites over the fields, seed genetics, county politics… and I know it sounds like I’m wandering.

People tell me, “You never answered what I asked,” and I get frustrated because in my head it all connects, but I guess I don’t always finish the first thought before I’m off on the next one.
Do you think your way of speaking has changed over time?

Yeah… I think it has. Or maybe folks just got less patient with me, I don’t know.

I used to be able to explain things straighter, like crop rotation or cattle prices, and people would follow me. Now when I try to explain the plan, it comes out all tangled—soil carbon, the bank men, satellites watching fields, seed genetics, county politics—and I’m trying to make the pieces fit, but people say I never get back to what they asked.

It’s frustrating, because to me it’s all connected. But I guess my talking has gotten harder for other people to follow.
Do you still hear the voices coming from the irrigation lines in the north pasture?

Yeah… I do. It’s mostly out by the north pasture, near dusk, when the light gets low and the water’s running through those lines. I can hear them clear, like voices coming right up through the irrigation pipes.

They’ll say which rows are poisoned and which ones are blessed, and I know that sounds… well, I know how it sounds. But it’s not just when I’m all wound up or fired up about things. It still happens on quieter weeks too.

And that north pasture’s always been strange anyway—the soil there never held water right after we reworked those rows, and the county man said it was drainage, but he didn’t listen about the lines—sorry. Yes. I still hear them.
Do you think your behavior on the tractor that day would have been different if you hadn't had anything to drink?

I don’t know if the drink was the main thing. Maybe it loosened me up some, but that wasn’t why they brought me in.

At the fair, during my talk, I climbed up onto the tractor because I was trying to show them the new pattern—how the controls had to move, how the rows line up if you do it right. And then I kept jerking the controls, demonstrating it, and people started yelling for me to stop.

I heard them, but I couldn’t quite make myself stop right then. It was like if I stopped before showing the whole pattern, nobody would understand it. So… maybe without drinking it would’ve looked different, I don’t know, but I still think I would’ve tried to show them.
Do you hear the voices from the irrigation lines when you're completely sober?

Yes. Sober too.

It’s not only when I’ve had anything. Out by the north pasture, especially toward dusk when the water’s moving through the lines, I hear them clear enough—like they’re coming right up through the irrigation. They’ll say which rows are poisoned and which ones are blessed.

And I know people want to make it about drink, or about me getting worked up, but it still happens on weeks when I’m not all fired up. That pasture’s always had trouble holding water anyway, after the rows were redone—well, I know that’s not what you asked. But yes, I hear them when I’m sober.
Do you often feel like your thoughts are racing or speeding by when you're trying to explain something to someone?

Yeah… yes, that happens a lot.

When I’m trying to explain something, my head gets going too fast—planting schedules, market prices, soil readings, all of it starts pushing in at once. And then there are things I feel like I’m supposed to make sense of, messages I need to decode, and before I can get hold of one thought, the next one shoves it aside.

So I’ll start telling someone one thing, and then I’m already three rows over in my head, thinking about the price of feed or whether the ground’s reading right, and I know I haven’t finished the first sentence. It’s frustrating, because I can see what I mean in my mind, but it runs ahead of my mouth.
Do you often find it hard to keep your thoughts in order when you're not trying to explain something to someone?

Yes… not just when I’m explaining, no.

Even sitting by myself, trying to make a plan for the day, it gets all tangled up. I’ll be thinking about soil carbon, then the bank men, then satellites watching the fields, then seed genetics, then county politics, and somehow it all feels connected, but I can’t keep it lined up straight.

And when somebody asks me one simple thing—like what’s the plan for planting—I start there, but I wander off and they say I never came back to the question. I don’t mean to do that. It just… it branches out faster than I can sort it.
Do you experience disjointed or disconnected thoughts when you are alone and not trying to communicate with anyone?

Yes… I do. Even when I’m alone, it doesn’t stay in a straight row, if that makes sense.

I’ll try to think through the plan for the day, and it comes out all tangled in my head—soil carbon, then the bank men, then satellites, seed genetics, county politics—and somehow I feel like it’s all part of the same problem. But if someone asked me later what I was thinking, I couldn’t lay it out clean.

It’s like when I try to explain the planting plan and people tell me I never got back to the question. I thought I did, but I guess I went around three other fields before I got there.
Do you think your way of thinking has changed over time, becoming more disorganized or harder to follow?

Yeah… I think it has. It used to be I could lay out a plan pretty plain—this field first, then that field, what seed, what day.

Now when I try to explain the plan, it comes out all tangled. I start with soil carbon, then I’m talking about the bank men, then satellites, seed genetics, county politics… and in my head it all belongs together, like pieces of the same map. But other people just look at me and say, “You didn’t answer what I asked.”

So yes, I guess it’s gotten harder for folks to follow me. Harder for me too, sometimes.
Do you think the voices from the irrigation lines would still be there if you stopped drinking altogether?

Yeah… I think they would. I mean, I’ve had weeks where I wasn’t drinking at all, and it still happened.

It’s mostly out by the north pasture, especially near dusk. I’ll be checking the irrigation lines, and I hear them clear as anything—voices coming through there, telling me which rows are poisoned and which ones are blessed.

And dusk is a funny time anyway, you know, the light lays different on the fields and the water carries sound strange, but… no, it’s not just the drinking. It still comes even when I’m not all fired up or anything.
Do you often have trouble expressing your thoughts in a way that makes sense to others?

Yes… pretty often, I guess.

I’ll be trying to answer something simple, like what my planting plan is, and I start with one thing—soil carbon, maybe—and then it runs over into the bank men, and satellites, and seed genetics, and county politics. In my head it’s all tied together, like irrigation lines feeding the same field, but people don’t hear it that way.

They’ll say, “You didn’t answer me,” or “Can you get back to the question?” And I thought I was getting there. I really did. It just comes out tangled.
Do you think your symptoms would be the same if you hadn't used any substances at all?

I don’t rightly know. That’s hard to separate out, like trying to tell which water came from which ditch after it’s already flooded the field.

I mean… I can say there’ve been times I wasn’t using anything and things still didn’t feel normal, but whether it would be exactly the same if I’d never touched any of it at all… I can’t say that. There’s weather, sleep, money pressure, family things—everything stacks up, you know?

So I guess my honest answer is I’m not sure. I don’t know how to untangle it cleanly.
Do you think your way of thinking would be clearer if you hadn't used any substances?

Maybe… but I don’t know that it would fix the whole thing.

When I try to explain the plan, it comes out all tangled. I’ll start meaning to talk about the field plan, and then I’m into soil carbon, and then the bank men, and satellites, and seed genetics, and county politics—because it all connects, you know? It’s all part of the same pressure on the farm.

But people look at me like I wandered off. They’ll say, “You never got back to what I asked.” I thought I did. I was trying to. So… maybe substances muddy it some, but the thinking itself still knots up on me.
Do you think the voices from the irrigation lines are real or just your imagination?

I… I don’t know if “imagination” is the right word, Doc. They sound real when I’m out there.

It’s mostly by the north pasture, near dusk, when the light gets low and the pipes start ticking and settling. I hear voices clear as somebody standing in the rows, coming from the irrigation lines. They’ll say which rows are poisoned, or which ones are blessed.

And I know that sounds… well, I know how it sounds. But it still happens even on weeks when I’m not all fired up or running high. I’ll be calm, just checking water, and there it is again. So it’s hard for me to call it just my imagination.

I’ll be trying to answer something simple, like what my planting plan is, and I start with one thing—soil carbon, maybe—and then it runs over into the bank men, and satellites, and seed genetics, and county politics. In my head it’s all tied together, like irrigation lines feeding the same field, but people don’t hear it that way.

They’ll say, “You didn’t answer me,” or “Can you get back to the question?” And I thought I was getting there. I really did. It just comes out tangled.

doctor.question: Do you think your symptoms would be the same if you hadn't used any substances at all?

target_item.reason: The question is asking whether the symptoms would persist without any substance use, which is about substance-related causation/exclusion. The provided symptom profile does not include a substance-use or substance-induced-symptoms item.

patient.answer:
I don’t rightly know. That’s hard to separate out, like trying to tell which water came from which ditch after it’s already flooded the field.

I mean… I can say there’ve been times I wasn’t using anything and things still didn’t feel normal, but whether it would be exactly the same if I’d never touched any of it at all… I can’t say that. There’s weather, sleep, money pressure, family things—everything stacks up, you know?

So I guess my honest answer is I’m not sure. I don’t know how to untangle it cleanly.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient's disorganized thinking is a persistent trait or a result of substance use
doctor.question: Do you think your way of thinking would be clearer if you hadn't used any substances?

target_item.name: Disorganized_Thinking_Speech

patient.answer:
Maybe… but I don’t know that it would fix the whole thing.

When I try to explain the plan, it comes out all tangled. I’ll start meaning to talk about the field plan, and then I’m into soil carbon, and then the bank men, and satellites, and seed genetics, and county politics—because it all connects, you know? It’s all part of the same pressure on the farm.

But people look at me like I wandered off. They’ll say, “You never got back to what I asked.” I thought I did. I was trying to. So… maybe substances muddy it some, but the thinking itself still knots up on me.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient's symptoms are consistent with a psychotic disorder
doctor.question: Do you think the voices from the irrigation lines are real or just your imagination?

target_item.name: Hallucinations
target_item.manifestation: Out by the north pasture, especially near dusk, I hear clear voices coming from the irrigation lines telling me which rows are poisoned or blessed, and it still happens on weeks when I'm not all fired up.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about the voices coming from the irrigation lines, which directly refers to auditory hallucinations and whether the patient experiences them as real.

patient.answer:
I… I don’t know if “imagination” is the right word, Doc. They sound real when I’m out there.

It’s mostly by the north pasture, near dusk, when the light gets low and the pipes start ticking and settling. I hear voices clear as somebody standing in the rows, coming from the irrigation lines. They’ll say which rows are poisoned, or which ones are blessed.

And I know that sounds… well, I know how it sounds. But it still happens even on weeks when I’m not all fired up or running high. I’ll be calm, just checking water, and there it is again. So it’s hard for me to call it just my imagination.
